title: csm-orchestrate approach fidelity, faults, functional gaps, and residual-limitations program: final three-pass report

tldr.content: Final verdict: csm-orchestrate matches the grill approach as a fail-closed controller prototype, but not as a production-complete outer loop. The right remedy is an authenticated assurance protocol around the controller: exact request-bound approvals, independent signal/review attestations, linearizable durable ownership/history, explicit unknown/cancellation states, executable remediation limits, and staged outcome evaluation. Do not enable production autonomy or claim improvement until those external boundaries are evidenced.

executiveSummary.content:
Three DEEP hybrid research passes were performed. Pass 1 compared the shipped implementation with the original grill approach and surveyed technical, host, and operability limitations. Pass 2 independently challenged those conclusions and corrected an optimistic trust model. Pass 3 adversarially reviewed both outputs, re-checked the repository, and narrowed claims where appropriate.

original approach -> pass 1 audit -> pass 2 challenge/remediation -> pass 3 adversarial review -> final decision-ready conditions

At commit d2fd905, the implementation has canonical JSON phase compilation, capability validation, typed handoffs, bounded local read-only scheduling, signal/requirement IDs, schema migration machinery, retry intent, receipt lineage, and a host-only final-review boundary. The unresolved issues are primarily semantic and operational: metadata is not proof, process-local coordination is not distributed durability, cancellation is not effect reconciliation, and tests are contract evidence rather than deployment evidence.

keyFindings.content:
K1. supported: The implementation matches the approach on canonical JSON authority, producer ownership, conditional route foundations, typed child lineage, fail-closed gates, bounded local scheduling, and durable-record interfaces [R1][R2].
K2. partially-supported: Evidence and acceptance-signal IDs now bind records structurally, but they do not prove semantic entailment; a producer can still assert a matching signal unless an independent validator evaluates the exact artifact [R3][R4].
K3. partially-supported: Final review fails closed without a host-issued marker, but the in-process marker and host response do not prove reviewer isolation, signer trust, or reviewer correctness; phase-level local review remains weaker [R1][R5].
K4. not-supported: Cross-process single ownership, exactly-once side effects, and completed cancellation are not supplied by process-local queues, maps, or AbortSignals [R6][R7].
K5. not-supported: Remediation budget consumption and physical insertedAfter ordering are not executable runtime invariants; activation predicates are descriptive rather than evaluated [R1].
K6. partially-supported: Schema migration and compatibility are substantially improved but require end-to-end semantic negotiation, not only field transformation [R3][R8].
K7. supported: Production rollout requires instrumentation, held-out deployment-like evaluation, independent blinded adjudication, contemporaneous control comparison, and tested rollback [R9][R10].
K8. supported: The defensible production contract is at-least-once execution with durable reconciliation, fencing, sink-side idempotency where possible, explicit UNKNOWN states, and fail-closed acceptance, not exactly-once arbitrary effects [R6][R7].

detailSections.content:
Approach differences and functional gaps: the original approach requires declared activation predicates to drive conditional routing, independent review for every material delegated output, bounded remediation, executable insertion ordering, approval binding to exact artifact digests, and long-horizon recovery. The code implements the structural representations but leaves several of those as metadata or injected-host responsibilities. `capabilityMatches` uses explicit signals and coarse text hints instead of evaluating manifest predicates. Final-review remediation validates insertedAfter but appends the phase. A positive remediation budget is checked but not atomically consumed.

Technical faults: ordinary approval binding covers skill digest and route identity but not the complete canonical request, exact input set, graph/policy revision, output contract, or retry identity. A process-local WeakMap write queue and terminal-invocation map cannot protect two coordinators from the same dispatch. Timeout and abort only end the controller wait; a side effect may continue and a retry may race it. Resolver references need immutable content-addressed snapshots and trusted namespace/attestation, not mutable paths plus assertions. The durable receipt must be backed by an event/history protocol if it is expected to reconstruct exact requests, cursor versions, late results, and ownership claims.

Minimum assurance protocol: canonicalize request R and compute requestDigest; obtain an audience-bound, one-time signed approval over R, input-set digest, graph/policy/validator digests, permissions, attempt, and expiry; atomically consume it while creating a fenced dispatch intent; have the host and reviewer attest to the exact request and immutable artifact snapshot; independently execute registered signal predicates; commit monotonic terminal state and complete history; classify timeout/cancellation as UNKNOWN until reconciled. Separate host attestation, reviewer attestation, signal appraisal, and relying-party acceptance.

Operational validation: instrument parent, phase, edge, child, attempt, approval, resolver, review, retry, cursor, and terminal events. Keep IDs in traces/logs rather than high-cardinality metric labels. Define SLI populations and denominators before thresholds. Use visible development, validation, held-out test, and post-deployment monitoring partitions. Start with deterministic/fault-injection tests, then shadow mode, isolated synthetic systems, and a small contemporaneous-control canary. Rollback must stop new dispatch, quarantine candidate outputs/approvals, reconcile in-flight effects, prevent cross-boundary retries, preserve history, and meet a measured rollback target.

recommendation.content: Retain the current controller architecture and keep it fail-closed. Address residual limitations in this order: 1) define an authenticated host/delegation and trust-anchor protocol; 2) bind approvals, attestations, resolver snapshots, validators, and receipts to one canonical request digest; 3) add a strongly consistent CAS/fencing/idempotency/history store and durable cancellation/reconciliation; 4) make activation predicates, remediation budgets, and graph insertion positions executable; 5) integrate traces, metrics, export-loss detection, and cost accounting; 6) evaluate a frozen, held-out, stratified workload with independent blinded adjudication; 7) run a bounded shadow/canary with absolute safety gates, control comparison, and tested rollback. Prefer a transactional outbox/inbox or durable workflow substrate when needed, but do not claim exactly-once arbitrary external effects without sink cooperation.

unverifiedClaims.content: Unverified: real host authentication and signer trust; reviewer process isolation and semantic correctness; approval issuer authenticity, revocation, and atomic consumption; authoritative artifact-index and immutable snapshot behavior; cross-process CAS/fencing/history; cancellation acknowledgement and late-result handling; sink-side idempotency/compensation; validator correctness and isolation; production workload representativeness; sample-size and confidence-bound choices; inter-rater reliability; causal improvement in accuracy, latency, cost, recovery, or human correction; canary/control isolation; and rollback completion under real faults. JSON Schema, signatures, trace digests, green CI, or agreement scores cannot establish these claims alone.

references.content: Local implementation claims are pinned to GitHub commit d2fd905. External references were retrieved on 2026-08-27 and include RATS, SLSA, OAuth security, JSON Schema, Temporal, Cloudflare Workflows, etcd, OpenTelemetry, Google SRE, NIST AI RMF, and Cochrane structured adjudication guidance.

claims.statement: At d2fd905, canonical JSON phase compilation, complete capability validation, typed handoffs, bounded local scheduling, fail-closed gates, schema migration machinery, and receipt lineage are implemented structural mechanisms.
Requirement and acceptance-signal identifiers provide structural binding but do not prove semantic entailment of artifact content.
The host-review path can reject unmarked local callbacks, but an in-process marker and host response do not prove host authentication, reviewer isolation, or semantic review correctness.
Process-local queues and maps cannot establish cross-process ownership, exactly-once arbitrary effects, or completed cancellation after timeout.
Activation predicates are not evaluated, remediation budgets are not consumed, and insertedAfter metadata does not control executable insertion position.
Approval and resolver trust must be bound to one canonical request and immutable content-addressed snapshot rather than separate asserted fields and mutable locators.
Production readiness requires correlated telemetry, predeclared SLI/SLO conditions, held-out deployment-like evaluation, blinded adjudication, contemporaneous control comparison, and tested rollback.
The defensible production contract is at-least-once execution with durable reconciliation, fencing, sink-side idempotency where possible, explicit unknown states, and fail-closed acceptance.
